title: Revelation Chapter 15 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Revelation chapter 15 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Revelation Chapter 15 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Revelation Chapter 15.

questions.question: In Revelation 15, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Seven angels having the seven last plagues
A sea of glass mingled with fire
Them that had gotten the victory over the beast
They sing the song of Moses
questions.correctAnswer: Seven angels having the seven last plagues
questions.explanation: This is the first event mentioned in the chapter, as stated in Revelation 15:1.

questions.question: What did the seven angels have in Revelation 15?
questions.explanation: This is directly mentioned in Revelation 15:1, where it states that the seven angels had the seven last plagues.

questions.question: What is mingled with fire in Revelation 15?
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:2 describes a sea of glass mingled with fire.

questions.question: Who stands on the sea of glass in Revelation 15?
options: Them that had gotten the victory over the beast
questions.correctAnswer: Them that had gotten the victory over the beast
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:2 states that those who had gotten the victory over the beast stand on the sea of glass.

questions.question: What do the victors hold in Revelation 15?
questions.explanation: According to Revelation 15:2, those who had victory over the beast hold the harps of God.

questions.question: What song do they sing in Revelation 15?
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:3 mentions that they sing the song of the Lamb.

questions.question: Who is referred to as the servant of God in Revelation 15?
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:3 refers to Moses as the servant of God.

questions.question: What are the works of the Lord described as in Revelation 15?
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:3 states that the works of the Lord God Almighty are great and marvellous.

questions.question: What are the ways of the Lord described as in Revelation 15?
questions.explanation: According to Revelation 15:3, the ways of the Lord are described as just and true.

questions.question: Who is referred to as the King of saints in Revelation 15?
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:3 refers to God as the King of saints.

questions.question: The angels are described as having what in Revelation 15?
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:1 mentions that the seven angels have the seven last plagues.

questions.question: In Revelation 15, the song sung includes the song of Moses.
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:3 states that they sing the song of Moses.

questions.question: In Revelation 15, the victors stand on a sea of glass.
questions.explanation: This is confirmed in Revelation 15:2 where it states they stand on the sea of glass.

questions.question: The text in Revelation 15 states that the angels sing the song of Moses.
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:3 indicates that it is not the angels but the victors who sing the song of Moses.

questions.question: In Revelation 15, the song of the Lamb is not mentioned.
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:3 explicitly mentions the song of the Lamb as being sung.

medium.title: Revelation Chapter 15 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Revelation Chapter 15 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who shall not fear thee, O Lord, and glorify thy name?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'for all nations shall come and worship before thee' (Revelation 15:4). This indicates that all nations will glorify God.

questions.question: What does Revelation 15:4 promise will happen if someone glorifies God's name?
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:4 presents that glorifying God's name is associated with not fearing Him.

questions.question: What did John see after the temple was opened?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'And after that I looked, and, behold, the temple of the tabernacle of the testimony in heaven was opened' (Revelation 15:5). This leads to seeing the seven angels.

questions.question: What does Revelation 15:5 indicate about the temple?
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:5 states that the temple was opened, which signifies access to God's presence.

questions.question: What were the seven angels wearing?
options: Clothed in pure and white linen
questions.correctAnswer: Clothed in pure and white linen
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:6 describes the angels as 'clothed in pure and white linen,' symbolizing holiness.

questions.question: What does Revelation 15:6 indicate about the angels' girdles?
questions.explanation: The verse mentions that the angels had 'golden girdles' which signifies honor and majesty.

questions.question: How does the song of Moses connect to Revelation 15:3?
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:3 states, 'Great and marvellous are thy works, Lord God Almighty,' showing how the song glorifies God.

questions.question: What are the victorious ones standing on in Revelation 15:2?
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:2 states that they stand 'on the sea of glass mingled with fire,' symbolizing purity and victory.

questions.question: What is revealed about God's nature in Revelation 15:4?
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly states, 'for thou only art holy,' emphasizing God's unique holiness.

questions.question: What is the significance of the seven last plagues mentioned in Revelation 15:1?
options: They are a sign of mercy
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:1 indicates that these plagues 'fill up the wrath of God,' signifying the completion of judgment.

questions.question: What are the harps used for in Revelation 15:2?
questions.explanation: The verse mentions that they have 'the harps of God,' indicating they are used to celebrate the victory over the beast.

questions.question: The judgments of God are made manifest in Revelation 15:4. What does this imply for believers?
options: They can trust in God's justice
They are to ignore the judgments
questions.correctAnswer: They can trust in God's justice
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:4 implies that knowing God's judgments are made manifest allows believers to trust in His justice.

questions.question: The statement 'Great and marvellous are thy works' indicates what about God in Revelation 15:3?
questions.explanation: This statement in Revelation 15:3 shows God's greatness and marvelous deeds, affirming His nature.

questions.question: The temple of the tabernacle of the testimony was closed in Revelation 15:5.
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:5 states that the temple was opened, not closed.

questions.question: The seven angels are described as having wings in Revelation 15:6.
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:6 does not mention wings; it describes them as clothed in linen and girded with golden girdles.

hard.title: Revelation Chapter 15 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Revelation Chapter 15.

questions.question: What did one of the four beasts give to the seven angels?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is found in Revelation 15:7, where it states that one of the four beasts gave unto the seven angels seven golden vials full of the wrath of God.

questions.question: What were the golden vials full of?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is found in Revelation 15:7, which states that the vials were full of the wrath of God.

questions.question: What filled the temple according to Revelation 15:8?
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:8 states that the temple was filled with smoke from the glory of God and from His power.

questions.question: Who was unable to enter the temple?
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:8 indicates that no man was able to enter into the temple until the seven plagues of the seven angels were fulfilled.

questions.question: How long does God live according to Revelation 15:7?
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:7 states that the wrath of God is from Him who liveth for ever and ever.

questions.question: What does the sea of glass represent in Revelation 15:2?
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:2 describes a sea of glass that signifies the purity and victory of those who overcame the beast.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'thymos' in Revelation 15:7 mean?
questions.explanation: 'Thymos' in Greek translates to 'wrath,' which is the content of the vials given to the angels in Revelation 15:7.

questions.question: What literary technique is used in Revelation 15:3 when referring to God's works?
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:3 employs parallelism in the praise of God's works, emphasizing His greatness and truth.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of God's wrath as seen in Revelation 15:1?
questions.explanation: Romans 1:18 discusses the wrath of God against all ungodliness, connecting with the theme found in Revelation 15:1.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the concept of victory over the beast stated in Revelation 15:2?
questions.explanation: 1 John 5:4 states that everyone born of God overcomes the world, echoing the victory over the beast in Revelation 15:2.

questions.question: What immediately precedes Revelation 15:7?
options: The seven angels coming out of the temple
The temple being filled with smoke
questions.correctAnswer: The seven angels coming out of the temple
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:6 directly precedes Revelation 15:7, describing the seven angels coming out of the temple with the plagues.

questions.question: What is the significance of the temple being filled with smoke in Revelation 15:8?
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:8 indicates that the smoke from the glory of God represents His divine presence and power.

questions.question: The seven plagues in Revelation 15:1 are also referred to as what?
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:1 refers to the seven last plagues, which are the final judgments of God.

questions.question: True or False: The vials given to the angels were filled with the mercy of God.
questions.explanation: The vials were filled with the wrath of God, as stated in Revelation 15:7.

questions.question: True or False: The temple was accessible to all men during the plagues of the angels.
questions.explanation: According to Revelation 15:8, no man was able to enter the temple until the plagues were fulfilled.

theological.title: Revelation Chapter 15 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Revelation Chapter 15 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Revelation 15:1 teach about God's nature?
options: God's wrath is a completed and perfect expression of His justice
God is indifferent to human sin
God's mercy overrides His justice in the end
God's wrath is arbitrary and unrestrained
questions.correctAnswer: God's wrath is a completed and perfect expression of His justice
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:1 states that in the seven last plagues is 'filled up the wrath of God,' indicating the fullness and perfection of God's just wrath.

questions.question: What doctrine about sanctification does Revelation 15:2 reveal?
options: Victory over the beast and his marks is an essential mark of the sanctified
Sanctification is a purely internal transformation with no external evidence
Sanctification removes believers from all trials
The sanctified are exempt from judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Victory over the beast and his marks is an essential mark of the sanctified
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:2 describes those who had 'gotten the victory over the beast, and over his image, and over his mark,' standing on the sea of glass, indicating that sanctification includes overcoming evil.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's judgment is taught in Revelation 15:4?
options: All nations will ultimately recognize God's holiness and worship Him because His judgments are manifest
God's judgments are hidden and inscrutable to all
God's judgments are limited to Israel only
God's holiness permits nations to ignore His judgments
questions.correctAnswer: All nations will ultimately recognize God's holiness and worship Him because His judgments are manifest
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:4 states that 'all nations shall come and worship before thee; for thy judgments are made manifest,' showing the universal effect of God's holy judgment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Revelation 15:6 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: The seven angels are 'clothed in pure and white linen,' symbolizing holiness, as seen in Revelation 15:6.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is exemplified in Revelation 15:8?
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:8 describes the temple filled with smoke from the glory of God and from His power, highlighting these divine attributes.

questions.question: How does Revelation 15:3 connect to themes elsewhere in Scripture?
options: It echoes the Old Testament song of Moses praising God’s mighty works and anticipates the new song of the Lamb in Revelation
It contradicts the Psalms by focusing only on wrath
It rejects the idea of worship in heaven
It limits God's works to earthly events
questions.correctAnswer: It echoes the Old Testament song of Moses praising God’s mighty works and anticipates the new song of the Lamb in Revelation
questions.explanation: Verse 15:3 explicitly mentions 'the song of Moses' and 'the song of the Lamb,' linking Old Testament worship with New Testament fulfillment.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme does Revelation 15:5 prepare for?
options: The opening of the heavenly temple as a precursor to divine judgment
The destruction of the earthly temple
The end of worship in heaven
The establishment of a new covenant on earth
questions.correctAnswer: The opening of the heavenly temple as a precursor to divine judgment
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:5 speaks of the temple being opened in heaven, preparing for the next stage of God's judgment revealed in the following verses.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Revelation 15:1 and 15:7 teach about God’s wrath?
options: God’s wrath is judicially executed through angelic agents who administer the final plagues
God’s wrath is symbolic and not literal
God’s wrath is limited to human emotions
questions.correctAnswer: God’s wrath is judicially executed through angelic agents who administer the final plagues
questions.explanation: Verse 15:1 introduces the seven angels with the seven last plagues as the fullness of God’s wrath, and 15:7 shows the angels receiving the golden vials full of God’s wrath for execution.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Revelation 15:2 and 15:4 teach about the worship and victory of the saints?
options: The saints’ victory over evil leads to universal worship of God due to His manifest judgments
Worship is independent of the saints’ victory
The saints will worship only in secret places
Victory over evil negates the necessity of worship
questions.correctAnswer: The saints’ victory over evil leads to universal worship of God due to His manifest judgments
questions.explanation: Verse 15:2 shows those victorious over the beast standing in worship, and 15:4 teaches that all nations will worship because of God's revealed judgments.

questions.question: What combined doctrine is taught by Revelation 15:6 and 15:8 regarding God's holiness and power in judgment?
options: God's holiness and power manifest in the purity of the angels and the overwhelming divine presence that prevents human access to the temple
God’s power is weak and His holiness is negotiable
Angels are unrighteous agents in judgment
Human beings can freely enter the temple during judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God's holiness and power manifest in the purity of the angels and the overwhelming divine presence that prevents human access to the temple
questions.explanation: Verse 15:6 describes holy angels clothed in pure linen, and 15:8 shows the temple filled with God's glory and power, blocking human entry.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Revelation 15:5-8 implies God is inaccessible during judgment. What does this passage actually teach?
options: God's temple is inaccessible to humans during the fulfillment of the seven plagues due to His overwhelming glory and power
God abandons His temple during judgment
Humans freely enter the temple to intercede during judgment
The temple is empty and inactive during the plagues
questions.correctAnswer: God's temple is inaccessible to humans during the fulfillment of the seven plagues due to His overwhelming glory and power
questions.explanation: Revelation 15:8 states no man could enter the temple until the seven plagues were fulfilled because of the smoke from God's glory and power.

questions.question: What doctrine does Revelation 15:7 teach about God's eternal nature?
options: God lives forever and ever, demonstrating His eternal sovereignty in executing judgment
God's life is limited to earthly history
God is subject to temporal constraints
God's existence is conditional on human faith
questions.correctAnswer: God lives forever and ever, demonstrating His eternal sovereignty in executing judgment
questions.explanation: Verse 15:7 explicitly states 'who liveth for ever and ever,' affirming God's eternal nature in relation to His judgment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is specifically demonstrated in Revelation 15:3?
questions.explanation: Verse 15:3 praises God as 'just and true,' highlighting His attribute of justice.

questions.question: What theological synthesis emerges from Revelation 15:2 and 15:6 about the role of angels in salvation history?
options: Angels serve as both worshippers and executors of divine judgment, reflecting God’s holiness and the victory of the saints
Angels are indifferent to human affairs
Angels only observe but do not participate in judgment
Angels replace the saints in worship
questions.correctAnswer: Angels serve as both worshippers and executors of divine judgment, reflecting God’s holiness and the victory of the saints
questions.explanation: Verse 15:2 shows victorious saints with harps (worship), and 15:6 depicts angels preparing to execute plagues, demonstrating their dual role.

questions.question: How does Revelation 15:4 contribute to the biblical doctrine of the universal scope of worship?
options: It teaches that all nations will ultimately worship God because His judgments are revealed and manifest
It limits worship solely to Israel
It teaches that worship is unnecessary after judgment
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that all nations will ultimately worship God because His judgments are revealed and manifest
questions.explanation: Verse 15:4 states 'all nations shall come and worship before thee,' emphasizing the universal nature of worship.
